title: The Bog Oak
text: A black oak trunk thousands of years old juts out of the peat like the prow of a sunken ship. The wood is hard as iron and dark as a starless night. Bog oak makes the finest bows in the world, the old bowyers say, and it is rarely found whole.

options.label: Dig the black trunk out of the peat, however long it takes.

outcomes.text: Black timber, hard as iron, heavy as guilt.
The bog wants it back, and you with it, and it pulls with all its patient strength.

options.label: The cleverest carves a bow from it on the spot, before the bog can take it back.

outcomes.text: A fine black bow, and a long afternoon, and the peat bubbling and sighing the whole time.

options.label: Leave it to the bog. It has kept the oak this long for a reason.

outcomes.text: It has waited this long. As you turn, the peat sighs and gives up a small thing it was keeping: a sliver of black wood, hard as iron, that the Leader binds to their weapon.
It has waited this long. It will wait for you too, the bog seems to say, and the Leader dreams of black water.

options.label: The one with a bow cuts a new stave from it, eager to see it sing.

outcomes.text: It takes all night and the bog does not like it, but the new limbs are black and hard as iron.
